title: Testing Business Ideas experiment inventory
page_numbering: PDF pages are 1-based; printed page = PDF page - 16 throughout this library.
classification_basis: Discovery and validation section inventories, PDF pages 120 and 250; variations counted separately.
use: Select for a specific hypothesis; the entries are not mandatory tasks and completion is not a validation certificate. Observation/limit and selection questions are local paraphrases/adaptations.
source_cautions: Some printed conversion formulas reverse exposures and actions; the note lists examples. Do not execute formulas without checking their definitions.
PDF pages 252, 256, 260, 264, and 270 have discovery headings inside the validation section; classification follows section inventories.
Pretend to Own, Card Sorting, and Buy a Feature also have subtype headings inconsistent with their inventory group.
Published thresholds, resource estimates, and case results are not universal success guarantees or current benchmarks.
Dot ratings are omitted rather than inferred from extracted text.

experiments.name: Customer Interview
experiments.observation_and_limit: Past experiences, jobs, pains, gains, workarounds, and rankings; favorable talk does not demonstrate future purchase.
experiments.selection_question: Which recent real episode can this customer describe?

experiments.name: Partner & Supplier Interviews
experiments.observation_and_limit: Capability discussions and bids address external delivery dependencies; a conversation does not establish reliable supply.
experiments.selection_question: Which needed activity or resource cannot we provide ourselves?

experiments.name: Expert Stakeholder Interviews
experiments.observation_and_limit: Internal expertise and organizational support; stronger follow-through matters more than approving quotes, and stakeholders are not customers.
experiments.selection_question: Whose knowledge or concrete support is missing?

experiments.name: A Day in the Life
experiments.observation_and_limit: Observe actual work and context before asking about it; contextual difficulty does not establish demand for our remedy.
experiments.selection_question: Can we observe the job where it normally happens?

experiments.name: Discovery Survey
experiments.observation_and_limit: Open-ended answers reveal themes for investigation; self-report and volunteer responses need follow-up.
experiments.selection_question: Which qualitative uncertainty can reachable respondents explain?

experiments.name: Search Trend Analysis
experiments.observation_and_limit: Search volume, geography, and changes over time expose interest patterns; search intent and offline demand remain uncertain.
experiments.selection_question: Does this audience express its problem through search?

experiments.name: Web Traffic Analysis
experiments.observation_and_limit: Existing traffic and funnel behavior reveal attention and drop-off; analytics show what happened more readily than why.
experiments.selection_question: Do we have relevant traffic and a meaningful funnel?

experiments.name: Discussion Forums
experiments.observation_and_limit: Complaints and actual workarounds expose problems; forum contributors are self-selected and feature requests are not purchases.
experiments.selection_question: Where does this audience already discuss its workarounds?

experiments.name: Sales Force Feedback
experiments.observation_and_limit: Deal records, calls, and sales observations surface obstacles; distinguish buyer evidence from salesperson interpretation.
experiments.selection_question: Can sales provide concrete wins, losses, and customer records?

experiments.name: Customer Support Analysis
experiments.observation_and_limit: Existing support cases reveal repeated needs and frustrations; complaint frequency alone does not prioritize a new solution.
experiments.selection_question: Is there enough relevant support history to find patterns?

experiments.name: Online Ad
experiments.observation_and_limit: Targeted impressions, clicks, and acquisition costs test message/channel response; clicking an ad is not buying.
experiments.selection_question: Can an ad reach this segment and lead to a meaningful action?

experiments.name: Link Tracking
experiments.observation_and_limit: Instrumented links reveal CTA response and subsequent behavior; click counts need eligible exposures and context.
experiments.selection_question: Which specific link action would teach us something?

experiments.name: Feature Stub
experiments.observation_and_limit: An unfinished feature entry point measures interest inside an active product; demand, usability, and implementation remain distinct.
experiments.selection_question: Can we expose and promptly explain an unavailable feature safely?

experiments.name: 404 Test
experiments.observation_and_limit: A deliberately unavailable destination produces error counts as an interest proxy; it can make the product appear broken.
experiments.selection_question: Is this short-lived, noncritical probe worth the disrupted experience?

experiments.name: Email Campaign
experiments.observation_and_limit: Opens, clicks, replies, unsubscribes, and downstream actions expose message response; email engagement is not revenue.
experiments.selection_question: Do we have a suitable list and one clear campaign objective?

experiments.name: Social Media Campaign
experiments.observation_and_limit: Posts generate reach, engagement, and possible conversions; attention and purchases carry different implications.
experiments.selection_question: Can this platform reach qualified people and track their next action?

experiments.name: Referral Program
experiments.observation_and_limit: Actual sharing, referred visits, and conversions test advocacy; incentives and acquisition do not establish retention.
experiments.selection_question: Do existing satisfied customers have someone relevant to refer?

experiments.name: 3D Print
experiments.observation_and_limit: A tangible model exposes physical reactions and constraints; customer feedback does not establish finished engineering or manufacturability.
experiments.selection_question: Is physical form necessary after cheaper sketches or models?

experiments.name: Paper Prototype
experiments.observation_and_limit: Observed tasks, confusion, and reactions test a rough interaction; limited paper sessions do not replace proper usability work.
experiments.selection_question: Can paper answer the interaction question cheaply?

experiments.name: Storyboard
experiments.observation_and_limit: Customer responses to illustrated experiences compare concepts; a team's storyboard alone is still a hypothesis.
experiments.selection_question: Which alternative customer experiences need comparison?

experiments.name: Data Sheet
experiments.observation_and_limit: Reactions to proposed specifications clarify requirements and partner fit; written specifications are not demonstrated capability.
experiments.selection_question: Which specification could change customer or supplier interest?

experiments.name: Brochure
experiments.observation_and_limit: Offline recipients' subsequent CTA actions test a proposition; accepting a handout or giving an email is limited commitment.
experiments.selection_question: Is this audience easier to reach offline?

experiments.name: Explainer Video
experiments.observation_and_limit: Views, sharing, and downstream actions test communication; a persuasive demonstration does not establish delivered functionality.
experiments.selection_question: Does motion explain the idea better than a simpler artifact?

experiments.name: Boomerang
experiments.observation_and_limit: Customers perform tasks with a competitor's real solution; observed shortcomings identify opportunities, not validation of ours.
experiments.selection_question: What can actual competitor use reveal about the unresolved job?

experiments.name: Pretend to Own
experiments.observation_and_limit: Living with a nonfunctioning model creates a usage/context log; imagination and self-use constrain conclusions about other customers.
experiments.selection_question: Can carrying or placing a model expose daily usefulness?

experiments.name: Product Box
experiments.observation_and_limit: Customers create and pitch imaginary packaging, revealing perceived benefits; attractive descriptions are hypothetical preferences.
experiments.selection_question: Which benefits would customers choose to explain to someone else?

experiments.name: Speed Boat
experiments.observation_and_limit: Customers identify obstacles and their severity; problem prioritization does not endorse the team's proposed remedy.
experiments.selection_question: What currently prevents progress, and which obstacle matters most?

experiments.name: Card Sorting
experiments.observation_and_limit: Sorting and ranking clarify jobs, pains, gains, and omissions; prompted rankings do not establish market behavior.
experiments.selection_question: Which priorities or missing concepts need clarification?

experiments.name: Buy a Feature
experiments.observation_and_limit: Constrained pretend budgets reveal trade-offs and negotiation; play currency is not actual willingness to pay.
experiments.selection_question: Which feature trade-offs emerge when everything cannot be selected?

experiments.name: Clickable Prototype
experiments.observation_and_limit: Clickable screens expose task performance and confusion; simulated interactions do not establish production usability or demand.
experiments.selection_question: Does the next uncertainty require interactive digital behavior?

experiments.name: Single Feature MVP
experiments.observation_and_limit: A functioning core feature supports payment, usage, satisfaction, and cost observations; one feature does not prove the whole business.
experiments.selection_question: Is earlier evidence strong enough to build this core function?

experiments.name: Mash-Up
experiments.observation_and_limit: Existing services combined into a working experience expose customer value and delivery cost; custom scaling remains untested.
experiments.selection_question: Can existing services deliver the experience without new infrastructure?

experiments.name: Concierge
experiments.observation_and_limit: Visible manual delivery reveals purchases, satisfaction, costs, and service timing; it does not establish scalable automation.
experiments.selection_question: Can people openly deliver the promised value manually?

experiments.name: Life-Sized Prototype
experiments.observation_and_limit: A physical service replica enables contextual reactions and CTA observations; realism and positive comments are not purchases.
experiments.selection_question: Must customers physically experience the setting to evaluate it?

experiments.name: Simple Landing Page
experiments.observation_and_limit: Qualified traffic responds to a proposition and CTA, often email signup; signups alone do not establish sales.
experiments.selection_question: Can we attract the right visitors and measure one meaningful action?

experiments.name: Crowdfunding
experiments.observation_and_limit: Financial pledges reveal stronger commitment; the book explicitly distinguishes this from proving technical feasibility or fulfillment.
experiments.selection_question: Can we make a credible offer and fulfill the promised rewards?

experiments.name: Split Test
experiments.observation_and_limit: Randomized control/variant outcomes compare a defined change; traffic, measurement, and stopping rules matter, and causes need interpretation.
experiments.selection_question: Is there enough relevant traffic to compare a prespecified effect?

experiments.name: Presale
experiments.observation_and_limit: Advance orders test an offer; this card charges when shipping, so order, collected payment, and fulfillment remain separate events.
experiments.selection_question: Is the product close enough to delivery to honor orders?

experiments.name: Validation Survey
experiments.observation_and_limit: Experienced users report disappointment, referral intentions, or rankings; stated sentiment is not retention or actual referrals.
experiments.selection_question: Have respondents recently experienced the product's core value?

experiments.name: Wizard of Oz
experiments.observation_and_limit: Hidden manual delivery yields payment, quality, cost, and timing observations; apparent automation does not prove technical feasibility.
experiments.selection_question: Can manual work test value before automation, with a defined transition trigger?

experiments.name: Mock Sale
experiments.observation_and_limit: A purchase attempt or payment-information submission tests commitment without processing payment; it is not a completed sale.
experiments.selection_question: Which uncharged purchase action would meaningfully test this offer?

experiments.name: Letter of Intent
experiments.observation_and_limit: Written intent from a prospective buyer or partner is stronger than casual interest; projected revenue is not collected revenue.
experiments.selection_question: Can a relevant decision-maker state concrete terms of intended engagement?

experiments.name: Pop-Up Store
experiments.observation_and_limit: A temporary venue exposes visits and selected commercial actions; location, novelty, and timing limit extrapolation.
experiments.selection_question: Can a temporary location test the intended buying experience?

experiments.name: Extreme Programming Spike
experiments.observation_and_limit: Timeboxed exploratory code tests a technical question against criteria; throwaway feasibility work establishes no customer demand.
experiments.selection_question: Which concrete technical unknown blocks the next decision?
